sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca mahāntam etam arthaṃ māṃ yaṃ tvaṃ pṛcchasi vismayāt tat pravakṣyāmi te sarvaṃ samādhāya manaḥ śṛṇu
english: Vyāsa said: This is a mighty matter on which, in wonder, you question me. I shall declare it all to you; compose your mind and listen.

sanskrit: yo 'sau nārāyaṇo nāma pūrveṣām api pūrvajaḥ ajāyata ca kāryārthaṃ putro dharmasya viśvakṛt
english: He who is named Nārāyaṇa, born before even the most ancient ones, was born for a purpose as the son of Dharma, the maker of all the world.

sanskrit: sa tapas tīvram ātasthe mainākaṃ girim āsthitaḥ ūrdhvabāhur mahātejā jvalanādityasaṃnibhaḥ
english: He undertook a fierce penance, stationed upon Mount Maināka, his arms raised aloft, of vast splendor, resembling fire and the sun.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣasahasrāṇi tāvanty eva śatāni ca aśoṣayat tadātmānaṃ vāyubhakṣo 'mbujekṣaṇaḥ
english: For sixty thousand years, and as many hundreds besides, the lotus-eyed one, feeding only on air, wasted away his own body.

sanskrit: athāparaṃ tapas taptvā dvis tato 'nyat punar mahat dyāvāpṛthivyor vivaraṃ tejasā samapūrayat
english: Then, having performed yet another austerity, and twice again another great one, he filled the gulf between heaven and earth with his splendor.

sanskrit: sa tena tapasā tāta brahmabhūto yadābhavat tato viśveśvaraṃ yoniṃ viśvasya jagataḥ patim
english: When by that penance, my son, he had become one with Brahman, he then beheld the Lord of all, the source of the universe, the master of the whole world —

sanskrit: dadarśa bhṛśadurdarśaṃ sarvadevair apīśvaram aṇīyasām aṇīyāṃsaṃ bṛhadbhyaś ca bṛhattaram
english: the Lord, exceedingly hard to behold even for all the gods, subtler than the subtlest and vaster than the vast,

sanskrit: rudram īśānam ṛṣabhaṃ cekitānam ajaṃ param gacchatas tiṣṭhato vāpi sarvabhūtahṛdi sthitam
english: Rudra the Ruler, the Bull, the all-perceiving, the unborn, the supreme, who whether men move or stand still abides in the heart of every being;

sanskrit: durvāraṇaṃ durdṛśaṃ tigmamanyuṃ; mahātmānaṃ sarvaharaṃ pracetasam divyaṃ cāpam iṣudhī cādadānaṃ; hiraṇyavarmāṇam anantavīryam
english: irresistible, hard to look upon, fierce in wrath, great of soul, the destroyer of all, the wise; bearing a divine bow and two quivers, clad in golden armor, of boundless valor;

sanskrit: pinākinaṃ vajriṇaṃ dīptaśūlaṃ; paraśvadhiṃ gadinaṃ svāyatāsim subhruṃ jaṭāmaṇḍalacandramauliṃ; vyāghrājinaṃ parighaṃ daṇḍapāṇim
english: wielder of the Pināka bow, of the thunderbolt, of the blazing trident, of the battle-axe, of the mace, of the long sword; fair of brow, crowned with the moon amid a circle of matted locks, clad in a tiger's skin, holding a bludgeon and a staff in his hand;

sanskrit: śubhāṅgadaṃ nāgayajñopavītiṃ; viśvair gaṇaiḥ śobhitaṃ bhūtasaṃghaiḥ ekībhūtaṃ tapasāṃ saṃnidhānaṃ; vayotigaiḥ suṣṭutam iṣṭavāgbhiḥ
english: adorned with fair armlets, the sacred thread a serpent across his breast, resplendent with all his hosts, the throngs of spirits; the one made whole, the very repository of austerities, well-praised with chosen words by those who have passed beyond age;

sanskrit: jalaṃ divaṃ khaṃ kṣitiṃ candrasūryau; tathā vāyvagnī pratimānaṃ jagac ca nālaṃ draṣṭuṃ yamajaṃ bhinnavṛttā; brahmadviṣaghnam amṛtasya yonim
english: whom water, heaven, the sky, the earth, the moon and sun, and wind and fire, and the measured world itself, cannot suffice to behold — the unborn one, whom those of perverse conduct cannot see, slayer of the foes of Brahman, the source of the deathless;

sanskrit: yaṃ paśyanti brāhmaṇāḥ sādhuvṛttāḥ; kṣīṇe pāpe manasā ye viśokāḥ sa tanniṣṭhas tapasā dharmam īḍyaṃ; tadbhaktyā vai viśvarūpaṃ dadarśa dṛṣṭvā cainaṃ vāṅmanobuddhidehaiḥ; saṃhṛṣṭātmā mumude devadevam
english: whom only Brāhmaṇas of holy conduct behold, who, their sin spent, are free of grief in mind. Devoted to him, through austerity and through love of him — that adorable, righteous one of universal form — he beheld him; and seeing him, with speech and mind and intellect and body, his soul thrilling, he rejoiced in the God of gods,

sanskrit: akṣamālāparikṣiptaṃ jyotiṣāṃ paramaṃ nidhim tato nārāyaṇo dṛṣṭvā vavande viśvasaṃbhavam
english: girded with a rosary of beads, the supreme treasure of all lights. Then Nārāyaṇa, beholding him, saluted the source of the universe —

sanskrit: varadaṃ pṛthucārvaṅgyā pārvatyā sahitaṃ prabhum ajam īśānam avyagraṃ kāraṇātmānam acyutam
english: the boon-giver, together with Pārvatī of broad and lovely form, the Lord, the unborn, the Ruler, the unperturbed, the very essence of all causes, the imperishable.

sanskrit: abhivādyātha rudrāya sadyo 'ndhakanipātine padmākṣas taṃ virūpākṣam abhituṣṭāva bhaktimān
english: Then the lotus-eyed one, full of devotion, having paid homage to Rudra, the slayer of Andhaka in an instant, began to praise that god of the strange-set eyes:

sanskrit: tvat saṃbhūtā bhūtakṛto vareṇya; goptāro 'dya bhuvanaṃ pūrvadevāḥ āviśyemāṃ dharaṇīṃ ye 'bhyarakṣan; purā purāṇāṃ tava deva sṛṣṭim
english: "From you, O most excellent, sprang the makers of beings, the elder gods who today guard the world, who of old, entering this earth, protected your ancient creation, O God.

sanskrit: surāsurān nāgarakṣaḥpiśācān; narān suparṇān atha gandharvayakṣān pṛthagvidhān bhūtasaṃghāṃś ca viśvāṃs; tvatsaṃbhūtān vidma sarvāṃs tathaiva aindraṃ yāmyaṃ vāruṇaṃ vaittapālyaṃ; maitraṃ tvāṣṭraṃ karma saumyaṃ ca tubhyam
english: Gods and demons, Nāgas, Rākṣasas and Piśācas, men, Suparṇas, and Gandharvas and Yakṣas, and all the manifold hosts of beings — we know them all alike sprung from you. The work of Indra and of Yama, of Varuṇa and of the Lord of Wealth, of Mitra and of Tvaṣṭṛ, and of Soma, is yours.

sanskrit: rūpaṃ jyotiḥ śabda ākāśavāyuḥ; sparśaḥ svādyaṃ salilaṃ gandha urvī kāmo brahmā brahma ca brāhmaṇāś ca; tvatsaṃbhūtaṃ sthāsnu cariṣṇu cedam
english: Form and light, sound, ether and wind, touch, the tasted, water, scent, the earth, desire, Brahmā, the Veda, and the Brāhmaṇas — all this, the unmoving and the moving, has sprung from you.

sanskrit: adbhyaḥ stokā yānti yathā pṛthaktvaṃ; tābhiś caikyaṃ saṃkṣaye yānti bhūyaḥ evaṃ vidvān prabhavaṃ cāpy ayaṃ ca; hitvā bhūtānāṃ tatra sāyujyam eti
english: As drops issue forth from the waters into separateness, and at dissolution return again into oneness with them, so the wise one, knowing both the origin and the passing of beings, leaves them behind and attains union there with you.

sanskrit: divyāvṛtau mānasau dvau suparṇāv; avākśākhaḥ pippalaḥ sapta gopāḥ daśāpy anye ye puraṃ dhārayanti; tvayā sṛṣṭās te hi tebhyaḥ paras tvam bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhavitā cāpy adhṛṣyaṃ; tvatsaṃbhūtā bhuvanānīha viśvā
english: The two birds, mind-born, wrapped in divine concealment; the pippala tree whose branches turn downward; the seven herdsmen, and the ten others who sustain the body's city — these were created by you, and beyond them all are you. What was, what shall be, and what is to come, unassailable — all the worlds here have sprung from you.

sanskrit: bhaktaṃ ca māṃ bhajamānaṃ bhajasva; mā rīriṣo mām ahitāhitena ātmānaṃ tvām ātmano 'nanyabhāvo; vidvān evaṃ gacchati brahma śukram
english: Cherish me, your devotee who cherishes you; harm me not by anything unfriendly. He who knows you as his very self, in undivided being, thus attains the radiant Brahman.

sanskrit: astauṣaṃ tvāṃ tava saṃmānam icchan; vicinvan vai savṛṣaṃ devavarya sudurlabhān dehi varān mameṣṭān; abhiṣṭutaḥ pratikārṣīś ca mā mām
english: I have praised you, longing for your favor, seeking you out together with your bull, O best of gods. Grant me the boons I cherish, hard though they are to win; and, thus extolled, turn me not away."

sanskrit: tasmai varān acintyātmā nīlakaṇṭhaḥ pinākadhṛk arhate devamukhyāya prāyacchad ṛṣisaṃstutaḥ
english: To him, the worthy chief of gods, the blue-throated wielder of the Pināka, whose nature is beyond thought, praised by sages, he granted boons:

sanskrit: nīlakaṇṭha uvāca matprasādān manuṣyeṣu devagandharvayoniṣu aprameyabalātmā tvaṃ nārāyaṇa bhaviṣyasi
english: The blue-throated one said: By my grace, O Nārāyaṇa, among men and in the wombs of gods and Gandharvas, you shall be of immeasurable strength of soul.

sanskrit: na ca tvā prasahiṣyanti devāsuramahoragāḥ na piśācā na gandharvā na narā na ca rākṣasāḥ
english: Neither gods nor demons nor great serpents shall prevail against you, nor Piśācas, nor Gandharvas, nor men, nor Rākṣasas,

sanskrit: na suparṇās tathā nāgā na ca viśve viyonijāḥ na kaś cit tvāṃ ca devo 'pi samareṣu vijeṣyati
english: nor Suparṇas, nor Nāgas, nor any of the misbegotten creatures of the world; not even a god shall ever vanquish you in battle.

sanskrit: na śastreṇa na vajreṇa nāgninā na ca vāyunā nārdreṇa na ca śuṣkeṇa trasena sthāvareṇa vā
english: Not by weapon, not by the thunderbolt, not by fire, nor by wind, not by the wet nor by the dry, not by the moving nor by the unmoving,

sanskrit: kaś cit tava rujaṃ kartā matprasādāt kathaṃ cana api cet samaraṃ gatvā bhaviṣyasi mamādhikaḥ
english: shall anyone, by my grace, ever do you injury in any way; and should you go to battle, you shall be greater even than I.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca evam ete varā labdhāḥ purastād viddhi śauriṇā sa eṣa devaś carati māyayā mohayañ jagat
english: Vyāsa said: Know that these boons were thus won of old by the heroic one. This same god walks abroad by his māyā, bewildering the world.

sanskrit: tasyaiva tapasā jātaṃ naraṃ nāma mahāmunim tulyam etena devena taṃ jānīhy arjunaṃ sadā
english: Born of that same one's austerity was the great sage named Nara, the equal of this god; know that one to be ever Arjuna.

sanskrit: tāv etau pūrvadevānāṃ paramopacitāv ṛṣī lokayātrāvidhānārthaṃ saṃjāyete yuge yuge
english: These two sages, most exalted among the elder gods, are born age after age to order the course of the worlds.

sanskrit: tathaiva karmaṇaḥ kṛtsnaṃ mahatas tapaso 'pi ca tejomanyuś ca vidvaṃs tvaṃ jāto raudro mahāmate
english: And likewise, O wise and great-minded one, from the whole of that great work and austerity were you born, fierce in splendor and in wrath, a very form of Rudra.

sanskrit: sa bhavān devavat prājño jñātvā bhavamayaṃ jagat avākarṣas tvam ātmānaṃ niyamais tatpriyepsayā
english: You, godlike and wise, knowing the world to be pervaded by Bhava, drew yourself inward through self-restraints, longing to win his favor.

sanskrit: śubham aurvaṃ navaṃ kṛtvā mahāpuruṣavigraham ījivāṃs tvaṃ japair homair upahāraiś ca mānada
english: Fashioning a fair and fresh image of the Great Person in the manner of Ūrva, you worshipped him, O giver of honor, with prayers, oblations, and offerings.

sanskrit: sa tathā pūjyamānas te pūrvadevo 'py atūtuṣat puṣkalāṃś ca varān prādāt tava vidvan hṛdi sthitān
english: That elder god, so worshipped by you, was well pleased, and granted you, O wise one, the abundant boons that dwelt within your heart.

sanskrit: janmakarmatapoyogās tayos tava ca puṣkalāḥ tābhyāṃ liṅge 'rcito devas tvayārcāyāṃ yuge yuge
english: The birth, the deeds, the austerity, and the discipline of those two and of you are alike abundant; by those two the god is worshipped in the liṅga, and by you in the image, age after age.

sanskrit: sarvarūpaṃ bhavaṃ jñātvā liṅge yo 'rcayati prabhum ātmayogāś ca tasmin vai śāstrayogāś ca śāśvatāḥ
english: Whoever, knowing Bhava to be of all forms, worships the Lord in the liṅga, in him are everlasting union of the self and union prescribed by scripture.

sanskrit: evaṃ devā yajanto hi siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ prārthayanti paraṃ loke sthānam eva ca śāśvatam
english: Thus the gods and the Siddhas and the supreme sages, by sacrificing, seek the highest and everlasting station in the world.

sanskrit: sa eṣa rudrabhaktaś ca keśavo rudrasaṃbhavaḥ kṛṣṇa eva hi yaṣṭavyo yajñaiś caiṣa sanātanaḥ
english: This very Keśava is both a devotee of Rudra and sprung from Rudra; Kṛṣṇa indeed is the one to be worshipped, and he is the eternal one to be honored with sacrifices.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtabhavaṃ jñātvā liṅge 'rcayati yaḥ prabhum tasminn abhyadhikāṃ prītiṃ karoti vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ
english: To him who, knowing Bhava as the source of all beings, worships the Lord in the liṅga, the bull-bannered god shows surpassing favor.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā droṇaputro mahārathaḥ namaścakāra rudrāya bahu mene ca keśavam
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing that speech of his, the son of Droṇa, the mighty car-warrior, made obeisance to Rudra and held Keśava in high honor.

sanskrit: hṛṣṭalomā ca vaśyātmā namaskṛtya maharṣaye varūthinīm abhipretya avahāram akārayat
english: His hair bristling with joy, his soul subdued, having bowed to the great sage, he turned toward the army and ordered the withdrawal.

sanskrit: tataḥ pratyavahāro 'bhūt pāṇḍavānāṃ viśāṃ pate kauravāṇāṃ ca dīnānāṃ droṇe yudhi nipātite
english: Then there was a withdrawal of the Pāṇḍavas, O lord of peoples, and of the stricken Kauravas, now that Droṇa had fallen in the fight.

sanskrit: yuddhaṃ kṛtvā dinān pañca droṇo hatvā varūthinīm brahmalokaṃ gato rājan brāhmaṇo vedapāragaḥ
english: Having waged war for five days and destroyed many a host, Droṇa, the Brāhmaṇa who had crossed to the far shore of the Vedas, went to the world of Brahmā, O king.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tasminn atirathe droṇe nihate tatra saṃjaya māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva kim akurvann ataḥ param
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When that surpassing car-warrior Droṇa had been slain there, O Saṃjaya, what did my men and the Pāṇḍavas do thereafter?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasminn atirathe droṇe nihate pārṣatena vai kauraveṣu ca bhagneṣu kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When that surpassing car-warrior Droṇa had been slain by the son of Pṛṣata, and the Kauravas were broken, Dhanaṃjaya, the son of Kuntī,

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā sumahad āścaryam ātmano vijayāvaham yadṛcchayāgataṃ vyāsaṃ papraccha bharatarṣabha
english: having beheld a very great marvel that brought him victory, questioned Vyāsa, who had come by chance, O bull of the Bhāratas:

sanskrit: saṃgrāme nighnataḥ śatrūñ śaraughair vimalair aham agrato lakṣaye yāntaṃ puruṣaṃ pāvakaprabham
english: "As I slew my foes in battle with floods of gleaming arrows, I marked before me a Person moving on, with the radiance of fire,

sanskrit: jvalantaṃ śūlam udyamya yāṃ diśaṃ pratipadyate tasyāṃ diśi viśīryante śatravo me mahāmune
english: holding aloft a blazing trident; and in whatever quarter he advanced, in that quarter my foes fell shattered, O great sage.

sanskrit: na padbhyāṃ spṛśate bhūmiṃ na ca śūlaṃ vimuñcati śūlāc chūlasahasrāṇi niṣpetus tasya tejasā
english: His feet touched not the ground, nor did he ever cast his trident; yet from that trident, by his splendor, thousands of tridents shot forth.

sanskrit: tena bhagnān arīn sarvān madbhagnān manyate janaḥ tena dagdhāni sainyāni pṛṣṭhato 'nudahāmy aham
english: All the foes broken by him the people deem broken by me; the armies consumed by him I do but burn over again from behind.

sanskrit: bhagavaṃs tan mamācakṣva ko vai sa puruṣottamaḥ śūlapāṇir mahān kṛṣṇa tejasā sūryasaṃnibhaḥ
english: Tell me this, O blessed one: who is that supreme Person, the great trident-bearer, dark of hue, in splendor like the sun?"

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca prajāpatīnāṃ prathamaṃ taijasaṃ puruṣaṃ vibhum bhuvanaṃ bhūr bhuvaṃ devaṃ sarvalokeśvaraṃ prabhum
english: Vyāsa said: It was the first of the Lords of Creatures, the Person of fiery splendor, the all-pervading, the very abode of being, earth and atmosphere, the god, the Lord and master of all the worlds —

sanskrit: īśānaṃ varadaṃ pārtha dṛṣṭavān asi śaṃkaram taṃ gaccha śaraṇaṃ devaṃ sarvādiṃ bhuvaneśvaram
english: the Ruler, the boon-giver, Śaṃkara, whom you have seen, O Pārtha. Go for refuge to that god, the origin of all, the Lord of the world —

sanskrit: mahādevaṃ mahātmānam īśānaṃ jaṭilaṃ śivam tryakṣaṃ mahābhujaṃ rudraṃ śikhinaṃ cīravāsasam dātāraṃ caiva bhaktānāṃ prasādavihitān varān
english: Mahādeva, the great of soul, the Ruler, the matted-haired, the auspicious Śiva, the three-eyed, the mighty-armed Rudra, crested, clad in rags, the giver to his devotees of boons granted in his grace.

sanskrit: tasya te pārṣadā divyā rūpair nānāvidhaiḥ vibhoḥ vāmanā jaṭilā muṇḍā hrasvagrīvā mahodarāḥ
english: The divine attendants of that pervading Lord are of forms manifold and various — dwarfish, matted-haired, shaven, short of neck, huge of belly,

sanskrit: mahākāyā mahotsāhā mahākarṇās tathāpare ānanair vikṛtaiḥ pādaiḥ pārtha veṣaiś ca vaikṛtaiḥ
english: and others vast of body, of great vigor, great of ear, with distorted faces and feet, O Pārtha, and with monstrous garbs.

sanskrit: īdṛśaiḥ sa mahādevaḥ pūjyamāno maheśvaraḥ sa śivas tāta tejasvī prasādād yāti te 'grataḥ tasmin ghore tadā pārtha saṃgrāme lomaharṣaṇe
english: Worshipped by such as these, that Mahādeva, the Great Lord, that splendid Śiva, my son, moves of his grace before you, O Pārtha, in that dreadful, hair-raising battle.

sanskrit: droṇakarṇakṛpair guptāṃ maheṣvāsaiḥ prahāribhiḥ kas tāṃ senāṃ tadā pārtha manasāpi pradharṣayet ṛte devān maheṣvāsād bahurūpān maheśvarāt
english: That army, guarded by Droṇa, Karṇa, and Kṛpa, mighty bowmen and smiters — who then, O Pārtha, could even in thought assail it, save the gods and the great bowman of many forms, the Great Lord?

sanskrit: sthātum utsahate kaś cin na tasminn agrataḥ sthite na hi bhūtaṃ samaṃ tena triṣu lokeṣu vidyate
english: None dares to stand his ground when that one stands before him; for no being is found equal to him in all the three worlds.

sanskrit: gandhenāpi hi saṃgrāme tasya kruddhasya śatravaḥ visaṃjñā hatabhūyiṣṭhā vepanti ca patanti ca
english: In battle, at the very scent of him when he is enraged, his foes, swooning and all but slain, tremble and fall.

sanskrit: tasmai namas tu kurvanto devās tiṣṭhanti vai divi ye cānye mānavā loke ye ca svargajito narāḥ
english: Doing him homage, the gods abide in heaven, and so do other men in the world, and those mortals who have conquered heaven.

sanskrit: ye bhaktā varadaṃ devaṃ śivaṃ rudram umāpatim iha loke sukhaṃ prāpya te yānti paramāṃ gatim
english: Those who are devoted to the boon-giving god, the auspicious Rudra, the lord of Umā, having won happiness in this world, go to the supreme goal.

sanskrit: namaskuruṣva kaunteya tasmai śāntāya vai sadā rudrāya śitikaṇṭhāya kaniṣṭhāya suvarcase
english: Pay homage, O son of Kuntī, to him, ever serene — to Rudra, the white-throated, the youngest, the radiant,

sanskrit: kapardine karālāya haryakṣṇe varadāya ca yāmyāyāvyaktakeśāya sadvṛtte śaṃkarāya ca
english: to the one of braided locks, the terrible, the tawny-eyed, the boon-giver, the kin of Yama, the one of unkempt hair, and to Śaṃkara of good conduct;

sanskrit: kāmyāya harinetrāya sthāṇave puruṣāya ca harikeśāya muṇḍāya kṛśāyottaraṇāya ca
english: to the lovely one, the green-eyed, the Pillar, the Person, the golden-haired, the shaven, the lean, and the deliverer;

sanskrit: bhāskarāya sutīrthāya devadevāya raṃhase bahurūpāya śarvāya priyāya priyavāsase
english: to the radiant as the sun, the holy ford, the God of gods, the swift, the one of many forms, Śarva, the beloved, the one in dear raiment;

sanskrit: uṣṇīṣiṇe suvaktrāya sahasrākṣāya mīḍhuṣe giriśāya praśāntāya pataye cīravāsase
english: to the turbaned, the fair-faced, the thousand-eyed, the bountiful, the dweller on the mountain, the wholly tranquil, the Lord clad in rags;

sanskrit: hiraṇyabāhave caiva ugrāya pataye diśām parjanyapataye caiva bhūtānāṃ pataye namaḥ
english: to the golden-armed, to the fierce, to the Lord of the quarters, to the Lord of the rain-cloud, and to the Lord of beings — homage!

sanskrit: vṛkṣāṇāṃ pataye caiva apāṃ ca pataye tathā vṛkṣair āvṛtakāyāya senānye madhyamāya ca
english: To the Lord of trees, and likewise to the Lord of the waters, to the one whose body is veiled by trees, to the army's leader, to the one in the midst;

sanskrit: sruvahastāya devāya dhanvine bhārgavāya ca bahurūpāya viśvasya pataye cīravāsase
english: to the god with the sacrificial ladle in hand, the bowman, the kinsman of Bhṛgu, the one of many forms, the Lord of all, clad in rags;

sanskrit: sahasraśirase caiva sahasranayanāya ca sahasrabāhave caiva sahasracaraṇāya ca
english: to the thousand-headed, and to the thousand-eyed, to the thousand-armed, and to the thousand-footed.

sanskrit: śaraṇaṃ prāpya kaunteya varadaṃ bhuvaneśvaram umāpatiṃ virūpākṣaṃ dakṣayajñanibarhaṇam prajānāṃ patim avyagraṃ bhūtānāṃ patim avyayam
english: Take refuge, O son of Kuntī, in the boon-giving Lord of the world, the lord of Umā, the strange-eyed, the destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice, the unperturbed Lord of creatures, the imperishable Lord of beings;

sanskrit: kapardinaṃ vṛṣāvartaṃ vṛṣanābhaṃ vṛṣadhvajam vṛṣadarpaṃ vṛṣapatiṃ vṛṣaśṛṅgaṃ vṛṣarṣabham
english: the braided-haired, whose course is the bull, whose navel is the bull, whose banner is the bull, the bull's own pride, the lord of the bull, the bull-horned, the bull among bulls;

sanskrit: vṛṣāṅkaṃ vṛṣabhodāraṃ vṛṣabhaṃ vṛṣabhekṣaṇam vṛṣāyudhaṃ vṛṣaśaraṃ vṛṣabhūtaṃ maheśvaram
english: the bull-marked, exalted as a bull, the bull itself, bull-eyed, whose weapon is the bull, whose arrow is the bull, who has become the bull, the Great Lord;

sanskrit: mahodaraṃ mahākāyaṃ dvīpicarmanivāsinam lokeśaṃ varadaṃ muṇḍaṃ brahmaṇyaṃ brāhmaṇapriyam
english: the vast-bellied, the great-bodied, clad in a panther's skin, the Lord of the world, the boon-giver, the shaven, the friend of holiness, dear to the Brāhmaṇas;

sanskrit: triśūlapāṇiṃ varadaṃ khaḍgacarmadharaṃ prabhum pinākinaṃ khaṇḍaparaśuṃ lokānāṃ patim īśvaram prapadye śaraṇaṃ devaṃ śaraṇyaṃ cīravāsasam
english: the trident-handed, the boon-giver, the Lord who bears sword and shield, the wielder of the Pināka, the one of the broken axe, the Lord and Master of the worlds — to that god, the refuge of all, clad in rags, I go for shelter.

sanskrit: namas tasmai sureśāya yasya vaiśravaṇaḥ sakhā suvāsase namo nityaṃ suvratāya sudhanvine
english: Homage to that Lord of the gods, whose friend is Vaiśravaṇa; to the well-clad, ever homage, to the one of holy vows, the bearer of the goodly bow;

sanskrit: sruvahastāya devāya sukhadhanvāya dhanvine dhanvantarāya dhanuṣe dhanvācāryāya dhanvine
english: to the god with the sacrificial ladle in hand, the one of the gladdening bow, the bowman, the one in the bow's interval, the bow itself, the master of archery, the archer.
